email.body1:
Zachary, saw Symetri expanded across the US with the TPM and Repro Products acquisitions, adding around 2,000 customers.

For your government business that means more in-market agencies in play than the team can cover before reps ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Symetri's government segment off hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Zachary, quick follow-up for Symetri.

As the government BD lead you feel coverage pressure first: more agencies and primes in play than reps can reach in a quarter, especially after two acquisitions. Most teams cannot actually say how many meetings they need to hit the number, so the gap shows up late.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your government segment needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Zachary, last bit of proof for Symetri.

Memgraph had more accounts in play than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how your segment's reply rate likely compares to peer technology resellers. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?

If scaling government pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Absorbing two acquisitions is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a government motion? I will tailor it to Symetri either way.
